title: Visual detection of pulselessness by carotid artery sonography – a prospective observational study among emergency physicians
summary:
The ultrasound examination of the carotid artery, which is easier to perform than echocardiography, could be a practical, quick alternative examination to differentiate between a pulse (as a surrogate parameter of kinetic cardiac activity) and its absence and help emergency physicians make decisions regarding the care of patients in cardiac arrest. 
The availability of sonography is also listed in the current guideline for supplementary "pulse detection" (pulse pressure wave - non-palpable pulse) and is optionally recommended in the European guidelines.

interventions.name:
Participating emergency physicians assess standardized, pre-recorded ultrasound video sequences of the common carotid artery. The video sequences are presented in B-mode, M-mode, and color Doppler and depict either the presence or absence of vascular pulsation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Consent of the participating emergency physicians
- Test persons must belong to the group of emergency physicians
- Sufficient visual acuity of the emergency physicians (self-assessment) to assess the video sequences
Exclusion criteria:
No existing consent of the test persons
- Test subjects do not belong to the group of emergency physicians
- Technical defect during presentation of the ultrasound sequences
